blocks.text: Mastering Zoom keyboard shortcuts for Mac

As a support lead, your hands should stay on the keyboard. Relying on the mouse to mute, share screen, or admit participants slows you down. Open Zoom, go to Zoom Workplace > Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts to view all available commands. Memorizing these changes how you handle meetings.

items: ⌘ ⇧ A: Toggle mute or unmute your audio.
⌘ ⇧ V: Start or stop your video.
⌘ ⇧ S: Start or stop screen sharing.
⌘ ⇧ H: Show or hide the meeting chat panel.
⌘ ⇧ W: Switch to gallery view or speaker view.

blocks.text: When you are in a high stakes meeting, you need information fast. If a customer asks a question you cannot answer immediately, do not fumble through browser tabs. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to find the relevant documentation in your internal knowledge base. Lazur will answer out loud, allowing you to stay focused on the customer.
Practical tips for support leads on Mac

Your Mac needs to be ready for back to back calls. Check your system permissions in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera and Microphone. Ensure Zoom is toggled on. If you experience performance issues, check if your Mac is running on battery power. Zoom performance improves when your Mac is plugged into a power source.

If you share your screen often, use a clean desktop layout. Hide unnecessary desktop icons to prevent sensitive customer data from being visible during screen shares. You can do this by right clicking your desktop and selecting Use Stacks.

blocks.text: Reducing meeting fatigue in support teams

Not every support issue requires a live call. Use asynchronous tools like Loom to record walk throughs for common customer problems. This saves your team time and allows customers to watch solutions on their own schedule. Reserve Zoom for complex escalations where real time interaction is required.

blocks.text: Common mistakes support leads make in Zoom

items: Forgetting to mute when taking notes on a loud keyboard.
Sharing the wrong window and exposing internal Slack channels.
Leaving the Waiting Room enabled during internal team meetings.
Running too many resource heavy apps alongside Zoom on older Intel Macs.
Failing to update Zoom, leading to compatibility issues with guest participants.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur while in a Zoom call on my Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur runs in the background. You can hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask questions or get help with your screen at any time, even while Zoom is active.

faq.question: How do I fix a black screen share in Zoom on Mac?
faq.answer: This is often a permission issue. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and ensure Zoom is enabled. You may need to restart Zoom after changing this setting.

faq.question: Does Lazur record my Zoom calls?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only sees your screen and hears your voice while you are actively holding the shortcut key. It does not record your meetings or store your audio.
